items.stem: In BPMN, what is the primary role of an exclusive gateway?

options.text: To route the flow down exactly one of several mutually exclusive paths
options.rationale: Correct: an exclusive (XOR) gateway selects a single path based on a condition.
That is the role of a start event, not a gateway.

options.text: To run several paths at the same time
To represent a task performed by a person
options.rationale: A task, not a gateway, represents work performed.

items.explanation: Correct: an exclusive (XOR) gateway selects a single path based on a condition.

items.stem: Which practices improve a BPMN process map? (Select TWO)

options.text: Placing each activity in the lane of the role that performs it
options.rationale: Correct: lanes make responsibilities and handoffs explicit.

options.text: Including exception paths, not only the happy path
options.rationale: Correct: real processes have exceptions that must be shown.

options.text: Keeping everything in a single lane for simplicity
options.rationale: This hides who does what and obscures handoffs.

options.text: Using events and gateways to mean the same thing
options.rationale: They have distinct meanings; conflating them breaks the model.

items.explanation: Correct: lanes make responsibilities and handoffs explicit.

items.stem: A reviewer praises a diagram as 'much nicer looking' though the underlying process still has the same delays. What misconception does this reflect?

options.text: A tidier diagram is not the same as an improved process
options.rationale: Correct: readability helps analysis but does not by itself fix the process.

options.text: Diagrams should never be made readable
options.rationale: Readability is valuable; it is just not the end goal.
BPMN can model timing and bottlenecks.
They can, but only when the actual flow changes.

items.explanation: Correct: readability helps analysis but does not by itself fix the process.
